overview: The ESP8266 was the board that first made 'a WiFi microcontroller for a few dollars' mainstream, years before the ESP32 existed. The NodeMCU dev board wraps the bare ESP8266 module with a USB-serial chip and a friendlier set of silkscreen pin labels (D0-D8) — but those labels are a trap: D1 is not GPIO1, it's GPIO5. Every NodeMCU pinout diagram has to be read carefully because the printed 'D' number and the actual GPIO number used in code are two different numbering systems.
simpleSummary: The original cheap WiFi microcontroller that made internet-connected projects affordable.

pinMap.name: D0
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO16). Can wake the chip from deep sleep.
pinMap.gotcha: No PWM/interrupt support, unlike the other D-pins — easy to forget since it looks identical on the silkscreen.

pinMap.name: D1
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O, common default for I2C SCL (actual chip pin: GPIO5).

pinMap.name: D2
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O, common default for I2C SDA (actual chip pin: GPIO4).

pinMap.name: D3
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO0), also a boot-mode strapping pin.
pinMap.gotcha: Must be HIGH at boot; a pull-down here prevents the board from starting normally.

pinMap.name: D4
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO2), wired to the onboard LED on most boards.

pinMap.name: D5
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO14), common SPI clock.

pinMap.name: D6
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO12), common SPI MISO.

pinMap.name: D7
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO13), common SPI MOSI.

pinMap.name: D8
pinMap.function: General-purpose I/O (actual chip pin: GPIO15), a boot-mode strapping pin.
pinMap.gotcha: Must be LOW at boot — the opposite requirement of D3/D4. A pull-up here breaks booting.

pinMap.name: RX (D9)
pinMap.function: Hardware serial receive (actual chip pin: GPIO3).

pinMap.name: TX (D10)
pinMap.function: Hardware serial transmit (actual chip pin: GPIO1).

pinMap.name: A0
pinMap.function: Analog input, 10-bit ADC, 0-3.3V thanks to an onboard voltage divider (the raw ESP8266 chip pin only accepts 0-1V).
pinMap.gotcha: Only one analog input on the whole board — budget carefully if a project needs multiple analog sensors.

pinMap.name: 3V3
pinMap.gotcha: WiFi transmit spikes can brown out a weak supply, same as the ESP32.

useCases.title: WiFi light/relay switch
useCases.scenario: The original 'IoT light switch' board — control a relay from a phone or web dashboard over WiFi.

useCases.title: Weather station uploading to the web
useCases.scenario: Read a BME280 over I2C and push readings to a cloud dashboard on a timer.

useCases.title: ESPHome / Home Assistant sensor node
useCases.scenario: Flash with ESPHome for a no-code integration into a home automation setup.

oftenConfusedWith: ESP32 (adds Bluetooth, dual-core, more pins, no D-number/GPIO mismatch)
